hints.title: Mandatory Cooldown State Transition Obstacle
hints.text: Selling stock introduces a mandatory 1-day cooldown period before another purchase can occur. How can tracking three distinct daily states (holding, sold, reset) navigate trading choices without violating the cooldown rule?

hints.title: Three-State Cycle Invariant
hints.text: Hold state transitions from hold or buying after rest. Sold state transitions from selling a held share. Rest state transitions from resting or recovering from a sale.

hints.title: Three Scalar Variable Machine Procedure
hints.text: Initialize hold to -infinity, sold to 0, and rest to 0. For each price p in prices, compute prev_sold = sold, update sold = hold + p, update hold = max(hold, rest - p), and update rest = max(rest, prev_sold). Return max(sold, rest).

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: number of days in prices
complexity.notes: Single linear pass updates three scalar state registers.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Simulating trade trees with cooldown takes O(2^N) exponential time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Constant scalar variables eliminate array allocation.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Modeling the problem as a 3-state finite state machine (Hold, Sold, Rest).
